entries.accessAssessment: Michigan GIS #119 and independent lower Slate River Falls locations agree, but the public visit route does not yet have permission-backed parking or a safe viewing path. UPtravel and Circle Tour describe a rough east-bank route from near the Skanee Road bridge. A separate field report required a river crossing for a close view and declined it during high water. The older Baraga visitor brochure's 3.3-mile Arvon Road/quarry directions overlap a different upstream Quartzite/Black Slate cluster. The Nature Conservancy now owns the 9,760-acre Slate River Forest, including approximately four miles of river, and permits hiking on ITS protected property, but published evidence does not prove the lower GIS #119 waterfall, road turnout and entire bank path are all on that property. An NBI-derived listing says the Skanee bridge itself is open, which does NOT authorize roadside parking. TNC separate Michigan land-use guidance states only 25% of Slate River Forest is currently enrolled in Commercial Forest and about one-third is covered by private hunting leases. Those figures govern hunting/fishing access analysis, not a determination that hiking is categorically prohibited elsewhere; parcel-specific rights and lease limitations must be read, and no walking line to the waterfall is authorized from these general sources. October 30, 2026 live public TNC ArcGIS Fee Ownership feature OBJECTID 8370 (Slate River Forest Reserve, PUB_ACCESS=Restricted Access) contains the exact state GIS Slate River Falls #119 coordinate 46.831054,-88.252067. The public Skanee Road bridge coordinates confirmed independently by USGS #04043165 and NBI #504 are OUTSIDE this TNC fee polygon. A diagnostic point roughly 100 m due east of the bridge and other sample points around the natural waterfall are inside the reserve. This is an actual TNC polygon/point intersection, not inferred from a place name. The polygon is generalized (maxAllowableOffset 0.00005°), not a parcel survey, road right-of-way, pedestrian easement, approved turnout, signed hiking route or safe dry-ground viewpoint. Visit Keweenaw's 2025 Hidden Gems article independently describes a small pull-off on Skanee Road after the bridge and a gorge-top hiking trail. It does not establish legal parking, a certified continuous path or a dry-ground waterfall viewpoint.

entries.accessAssessment: FERC's December 29, 2025 final order (Docket P-10856-141, 193 FERC ¶61,242) TERMINATED the Au Train Hydroelectric Project license by implied surrender, effective that day's close of business, with existing facilities LEFT IN PLACE. FERC's record cites high-hazard dam classification, inadequate spillway remediation, licensee UP Hydro's bankruptcy and loss of property control. In 2025 foreclosure, Stephenson Bank acquired 18/22 project parcels and later sold those 18 to D. Charles Trust Investments, LLC (including powerhouse and surrounding project buffer), but individual tourist parking and falls-side parcel title/right of way are not mapped by this order. Michigan EGLE now holds state dam-safety jurisdiction; termination neither orders immediate dam removal nor establishes all waterfall visitor routes closed or open. Munising tourism describes two separate upper/lower falls visitor stops near utility gates, but that older guidance does not establish October 2026 parking, public gate entry, walkway, flow conditions or new property owner consent.
